page: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit arm64 AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processor. Operating at 2.6 GHz, the configuration supplies 16 physical cores with one thread per core, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Total system memory measures 32.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. The server features no bundled local storage, contains no GPU accelerators, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate steady mid-tier compute capabilities alongside strong memory throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1,480.0 and a multi-core score of 12,798.0, with clang software compilation reaching 20,737.0. Uncached large-block memory write throughput reaches a strong 93.97 GB/sec, reflected in a PassMark memory score of 2,972.27. The PassMark CPU score registers at 11,483.62, though encryption performance falls into the lower quartile at 2,226.35. In application tests, Redis SET throughput reaches 26.15 million operations per second, static web serving measures 28.48 GB/sec, and 7B model prompt processing executes at 28.19 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by the power-efficient Graviton3 microarchitecture, delivering dedicated physical cores that avoid hyperthreading resource contention. Operational tradeoffs include reliance on external network storage due to the absence of local disks and the requirement for software compatibility with ARMv8 instruction sets. This instance suits distributed code compilation, batch computing, containerized microservices, static web traffic, and caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by 16 dedicated AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 cores running at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features a 1:2 compute-to-memory profile with 32.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In synthetic evaluations, it demonstrates consistent execution with a PassMark CPU score of 11,483.62, a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,798.0, and strong memory write throughput of 93.97 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput reaches 26.15 million operations per second, and static web serving hits 28.48 GB/sec, though PassMark encryption testing falls in the lower percentile. Operating on dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, c7g.4xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, distributed container clusters, batch compute workloads, and web serving deployments targeting arm64 environments.
